title: Genital warts: care without blame
intro: Genital warts are caused mainly by low-risk human papillomavirus types. These differ from the types responsible for most cancers, but different types may coexist and appropriate cervical screening remains important.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Bumps around the genitals or anus may itch or bleed. Not every bump is a wart; infection can precede visible growths by a long time, so appearance cannot date transmission.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: A clinician examines the area and may biopsy unusual, dark, ulcerated or unresponsive lesions. Discuss pregnancy, immune suppression and other sexually transmitted infection tests confidentially. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Prescribed creams, freezing and removal procedures are options; some warts resolve without treatment and recurrence is possible. Never apply ordinary hand-wart acids to genital skin. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Avoid picking or shaving over growths and follow application instructions. Condoms reduce but do not eliminate HPV transmission. Vaccination prevents covered infections but does not treat existing warts. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Review rapidly growing, persistently bleeding or ulcerated lesions and major treatment irritation. Pregnancy changes suitable medicines. Continue recommended cervical screening after vaccination or wart treatment.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira asks about vaccination after treatment. She understands that it can prevent covered infections without erasing the current infection.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben books an examination for a dark bleeding bump instead of applying a hand-wart remover to genital skin.
